key_insight: ATLAS learns a diffusion-based sampler that can generate Boltzmann-distributed amorphous structures and estimate thermodynamics efficiently, even in hard-to-equilibrate glassy regimes.
engineering_relevance: It could substantially reduce the cost of simulating, characterizing, and inverse-designing metallic glasses and other amorphous materials with target mechanical or functional properties.
method: Equivariant graph neural network parameterizes the reverse diffusion process from a target energy function.
Supports sampling, free-energy/entropy estimation, and steering toward desired observables via time-reversal of diffusion.
Uses composition-amortized pretraining to transfer across system size, temperature, composition, and expensive interatomic potentials.
evidence_signal: In 2D Kob-Andersen systems, ATLAS matched parallel tempering MCMC distributions and achieved below 0.2% free-energy error in the low-temperature glass regime with over 500× fewer energy evaluations.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and coverage of the learned energy model and pretraining data, so extrapolation to unseen chemistries or observables may still require careful validation.
paper_title: ATLAS: A Foundation Neural Sampler for Amorphous Materials
